evidence.claim: Buhari said weapons from the Ukraine-Russia war were beginning to filter into the Lake Chad Basin, but VOA's fact check found the claim unsubstantiated and noted there were no public reports or evidence supporting it.

evidence.claim: Buhari framed 2022 tax policy around stable domestic revenue mobilization, tax harmonization, clearer FIRS authority, and improved tax-to-GDP performance, while saying the 2021 tax dialogue influenced policy and administrative changes and FIRS surpassed its 2021 collection target.

evidence.claim: Buhari said his administration's fight against corruption was a cardinal reform pillar and linked the Open Government Partnership to transparency in public finances and procurement, while urging ICPC action on sexual harassment in education.

Other evidence shows ongoing corruption and fiscal leakage.

evidence.claim: WHO said Nigeria had over 2.3 million zero-dose children in 2022 and that the government prioritized reaching them through its national immunization and primary health care strategy, while over six million children benefited from immunization services between March 2021 and January 2023.

evidence.claim: Headline inflation was 21.34% in December 2022, up 5.72 percentage points year-on-year from December 2021, showing continued price deterioration by year-end.

Inflation was also driven by food and exchange-rate pressures outside direct presidential control.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said Nigeria spent only about $220 per person in 2022, social sectors received less than a quarter of the national budget, and regressive fuel, electricity, and exchange-rate subsidies diverted resources away from social services and infrastructure.

contrary_evidence: The administration did try to raise revenue and improve service delivery.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Nigeria's crude output fell below 1 million barrels per day in August 2022 because of rampant pipeline theft and years of underinvestment, threatening public finances.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that NNPC spent 4.39 trillion naira on petrol subsidy in 2022, did not remit funds to federal accounts, and that the subsidy left a hole in public finances while oil production remained constrained by theft and vandalism.

evidence.claim: ASUU suspended its eight-month strike after appeals from President Buhari and others, and Reuters noted the government had set aside 470 billion naira for salary enhancements in tertiary institutions.

evidence.claim: UNICEF said the 2022 floods left more than 2.5 million people in Nigeria needing humanitarian assistance, displaced 1.3 million, killed over 600, and damaged over 200,000 homes.
evidence.title: More than 1.5 million children at risk as devastating floods hit Nigeria

The magnitude is partly a weather and climate shock, not a governance choice.

evidence.claim: Buhari approved Ahmed Halilu as substantive managing director of the Nigerian Security Printing and Minting Company, after Halilu had served in an acting role; the report says the appointment followed a CBN governor recommendation.

evidence.claim: The report says Ahmed Halilu, the elder brother to First Lady Aisha Buhari, was appointed managing director of NSPMC and that Buhari made the appointment permanent after Halilu had acted since May 16, 2022.
evidence.title: Buhari appoints brother-in-law, Ahmed Halilu, to head Nigeria's currency printing company
